rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding ~0.5 at% Hf to promote Hf-rich precipitates, while the target paper added 4.2 at% Cr to form a Laves phase. These are different elements, different amounts, and different intended phase formations, representing a different specific lever.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature testing (1000–1123 K) and room-temperature tests, while the target paper performed only room-temperature compression testing. The temperature regimes are different, though both include room-temperature testing.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes precipitation strengthening from Hf-rich particles impeding dislocations and grain boundaries, while the target paper describes a dual mechanism of solid solution hardening and crack hindrance from a reticulated Laves phase. These are different general classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved high-temperature strength and ductility with preserved room-temperature performance, while the target paper reports concurrent increases in room-temperature yield strength and fracture strain. The property (mechanical performance) and direction (improvement) are the same, but the temperature regime differs.
